mostWorthwhile.text: Making and exporting collagen was most worthwhile: the sequence connects instructions and amino acids inside a cell to support fibers outside it. The described panels make that connection clear, although finished images are not available to assess.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the finished fibers to the body was a predictable fitting step, though it clearly showed which part of the wound had been repaired.

surprise.text: The closed surface did not mean the deeper repair was finished; the collagen still needed remodeling and strengthening.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The local repair signals were a plausible prompt for the edge cells, though I was inferring their precise role before combining them.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it similarly connected cell activity to a visible change in the body. The repair sequence was clear, although most choices were fairly predictable.
